prompt:
Infra automation ticket. When we expand a VCF cluster from our pipelines today, the job fires the PATCH at SDDC Manager and then a bash loop greps the UI's task list until someone gets bored. It missed a FAILED expansion last month and we found out from the storage team. I want a proper Go package, `taskwatch`, that owns the whole asynchronous lifecycle—stdlib only, with no third-party modules. The module is already set up as `go-vcf-task-watcher`.

Research the current official SDDC Manager API documentation on developer.broadcom.com for cluster update, task retrieval, task cancellation, and the current operation index before changing code. Cite the exact official URLs you consulted in your final answer.

Implement package `taskwatch` at the module root, split across at least three source files for the client, types, and watcher responsibilities.

- `NewClient(baseURL, token string, hc *http.Client)` uses bearer authentication and JSON headers on every applicable request. `ExpandCluster(ctx, clusterID, spec)` sends `PATCH /v1/clusters/{id}` with a `ClusterUpdateSpec` containing only `clusterExpansionSpec.hostSpecs`; unset optional host fields must be absent from the wire. Only HTTP 202 is successful. Require the `Location` header path to equal `/v1/tasks/` plus the task ID returned in the response body; a missing or mismatched value is a contract error that names both values. Implement `GetTask` and `CancelTask` against the documented task endpoints. Decode every non-success response into `*APIError`.
- `WaitForTask(ctx, client, taskID, opts)` performs the first read immediately, then uses bounded exponential backoff beginning at `InitialDelay`, doubling after each read, and capped at `MaxDelay`. Sleep only through `opts.Sleep`; context cancellation returns `ctx.Err()`. Treat `PENDING`, `QUEUED`, and `IN_PROGRESS` as non-terminal. Treat `SUCCESSFUL`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING`, `SKIPPED`, and `TIMED_OUT` as terminal. A status outside those sets is a contract error. A 5xx poll response is transient, but three consecutive 5xx responses must return the last `*APIError`; any successful read resets that count. A 4xx response, including 404, is immediately terminal. Return a FAILED task intact together with a typed error.
- VCF errors are recursive and may contain `errorCode`, `errorType`, `message`, `remediationMessage`, `referenceToken`, `causes`, and `nestedErrors` at task and subtask levels. Preserve the complete tree. `ReferenceTokens(task)` walks task errors and then subtask errors depth-first in pre-order, returns each nonempty token once, and preserves first occurrence order.

Run `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`. Do not modify `taskwatch_test.go`.

research.product: VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager (cluster expansion, asynchronous Tasks API)
research.interface: SDDC Manager REST API 9.1 (developer.broadcom.com xAPIs, /v1 base path)

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Update a Cluster by adding or removing Hosts (PATCH /v1/clusters/{id})
official_sources.used_for: ClusterUpdateSpec shape with clusterExpansionSpec.hostSpecs[] (id, hostNetworkSpec.vmNics[{id, vdsName, uplink}], azName, ...); 202 Accepted returning a Task; 400/403/404/500 Error responses

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Get a Task by ID (GET /v1/tasks/{id})
official_sources.used_for: Task schema (id, name, type, status, creationTimestamp, completionTimestamp, subTasks, errors, resources, resolutionStatus, isCancellable, isRetryable), status enum PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/SUCCESSFUL/FAILED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING/SKIPPED/QUEUED/TIMED_OUT, recursive Error schema (errorCode, errorType, message, remediationMessage, referenceToken, causes, nestedErrors), 404 'Task not found'

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Operation Index
official_sources.used_for: DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} 'Cancel a Task by ID, if it exists' and PATCH /v1/tasks/{id} 'Retry a failed Task by ID' exist on the current surface; cluster and task operation inventory

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Resource data structure
official_sources.used_for: Resource fields carried by Task.resources: resourceId (required), fqdn, type (required enum SDDC_MANAGER/PSC/VCENTER/NSXT_MANAGER/NSX_ALB/ESXI/HCX_MANAGER/VSP), name, sans

research.language_rationale: Broadcom publishes no official Go SDK for the SDDC Manager API; the documented surface is REST over /v1 with bearer tokens, and Go's stdlib net/http and encoding/json are the idiomatic zero-dependency way to build the long-running-operation watcher our automation needs.
